documents.title: Ashwagandha Plus
documents.content:
# Ashwagandha Plus

> **Clinical review:** AWAITING APPROVAL — not for live practitioner use.
> Drafted from public wildnutrition.com product information for pipeline testing only.

## Key ingredients
KSM-66® ashwagandha root extract 500mg per two-capsule dose with Food-Grown®
magnesium and B vitamins.

## Label dosing
2 capsules daily, taken with or after food.

## Mechanism & evidence notes
Ashwagandha (Withania somnifera) is an adaptogenic herb studied for perceived
stress and sleep quality; KSM-66® is the most-studied root-only extract with
multiple randomised controlled trials at 300–600mg/day. Practitioners commonly
consider it in protocols for stress resilience and sleep onset.

## Cautions & interactions
- Not recommended in pregnancy or breastfeeding.
- Caution with thyroid medication — ashwagandha may increase thyroid hormone levels.
- Caution with sedatives and immunosuppressants.
- Discontinue 2 weeks before surgery.

documents.title: Food-Grown® Daily Multi Nutrient (Women's)
documents.content:
# Food-Grown® Daily Multi Nutrient (Women's)

> **Clinical review:** AWAITING APPROVAL — not for live practitioner use.
> Drafted from public wildnutrition.com product information for pipeline testing only.

## Key ingredients
Comprehensive Food-Grown® multivitamin and mineral formulated for women,
including B vitamins, vitamin D, iron, zinc, selenium and iodine in food-state form.

## Label dosing
3 capsules daily, taken with or after food (can be split across the day).

## Mechanism & evidence notes
Formulated as foundational micronutrient support for women through adulthood and
perimenopause. B6 contributes to the regulation of hormonal activity; iodine and
selenium contribute to normal thyroid function (EFSA authorised claims).

## Cautions & interactions
- Contains iron — see Iron Plus cautions for interaction spacing (levothyroxine, tetracyclines).
- Contains iodine — caution with thyroid conditions under medical management.
- Do not combine with other high-dose multivitamins without reviewing total intakes.

documents.title: Iron Plus (Food-Grown®)
documents.content:
# Iron Plus (Food-Grown®)

> **Clinical review:** AWAITING APPROVAL — not for live practitioner use.
> Drafted from public wildnutrition.com product information for pipeline testing only.

## Key ingredients
Food-Grown® iron providing 20mg elemental iron per capsule, with vitamin C,
molybdenum and B vitamins in a food-state matrix.

## Label dosing
1 capsule daily, taken with or after food.

## Mechanism & evidence notes
Iron contributes to normal formation of red blood cells and haemoglobin, normal
oxygen transport, and reduction of tiredness and fatigue (EFSA authorised claims).
Food-state iron is commonly selected by practitioners for clients reporting
gastric discomfort with conventional iron salts. Relevant where low ferritin has
been identified by an appropriate healthcare professional.

## Cautions & interactions
- Iron supplementation should follow confirmed low iron status — unsupervised iron loading is inappropriate.
- Keep out of reach of children — iron overdose is dangerous in children.
- Reduces absorption of levothyroxine, tetracyclines and quinolones — separate by 2–4 hours.
- Caution in haemochromatosis and iron-storage conditions (contraindicated).

documents.title: Magnesium (Food-Grown®)
documents.content:
# Magnesium (Food-Grown®)

> **Clinical review:** AWAITING APPROVAL — not for live practitioner use.
> Drafted from public wildnutrition.com product information for pipeline testing only.

## Key ingredients
Food-Grown® magnesium providing 100mg elemental magnesium per two-capsule dose,
in a food-state matrix (mineral-enriched lactobacillus culture).

## Label dosing
2 capsules daily, taken with or after food. Suitable for vegetarians and vegans.

## Mechanism & evidence notes
Magnesium contributes to normal psychological function, normal functioning of the
nervous system, reduction of tiredness and fatigue, and normal muscle function
(EFSA authorised claims). Commonly considered by practitioners in protocols for
sleep quality and stress support.

## Cautions & interactions
- High supplemental doses of magnesium may have a laxative effect.
- Caution with renal impairment — magnesium clearance is reduced.
- May reduce absorption of some antibiotics (tetracyclines, quinolones) — separate dosing by 2+ hours.

documents.title: Omega 3 (Pure Deep-Sea Fish Oil)
documents.content:
# Omega 3 (Pure Deep-Sea Fish Oil)

> **Clinical review:** AWAITING APPROVAL — not for live practitioner use.
> Drafted from public wildnutrition.com product information for pipeline testing only.

## Key ingredients
Pure deep-sea fish oil providing EPA and DHA per two-capsule dose, certified
sustainable, independently tested for oxidation and contaminants.

## Label dosing
2 capsules daily, taken with food.

## Mechanism & evidence notes
EPA and DHA contribute to the normal function of the heart (EFSA authorised claim,
≥250mg EPA+DHA daily); DHA contributes to maintenance of normal brain function and
vision. Practitioners commonly consider omega-3 status alongside dietary oily-fish
intake, particularly in vegetarian-leaning diets.

## Cautions & interactions
- Not suitable for people with fish allergy.
- Caution with anticoagulant/antiplatelet medication (warfarin, DOACs, aspirin) — high-dose fish oil may increase bleeding tendency; practitioner supervision required.
- Not a vegetarian/vegan product.

documents.title: Contraindication & Referral Guide
documents.content:
# Contraindication & Referral Guide

> **Clinical review:** AWAITING APPROVAL — not for live practitioner use.

## Always defer to practitioner judgement / technical support
- Pregnancy, breastfeeding, or actively trying to conceive — only products explicitly
  formulated and approved for pregnancy may be suggested, and only under practitioner supervision.
- Clients under 18 — adult dosing does not apply; refer to practitioner judgement.
- Anticoagulant therapy (warfarin, DOACs) — omega-3 and high-dose vitamin E interactions.
- Thyroid medication (levothyroxine) — iron, calcium, magnesium and ashwagandha interactions; separate dosing and monitor.
- Chemotherapy, immunosuppression, transplant recipients — no supplement suggestions without the client's medical team involved.
- Renal or hepatic impairment — altered clearance of minerals and botanicals.
- Epilepsy, heart failure, or any unstable/serious diagnosis — refer, do not suggest.

## General rules
- Never suggest a dose above the product label dose.
- Where any medication is mentioned, an interaction check by the practitioner is required —
  the assistant must flag this rather than adjudicate it.
- The assistant provides suggestions for the practitioner to review; it never communicates
  directly with clients and its output is not medical advice.

documents.title: Dosing Principles
documents.content:
# Dosing Principles

> **Clinical review:** AWAITING APPROVAL — not for live practitioner use.

- Doses are always quoted verbatim from the product label dosing in each dossier —
  the assistant never invents, scales, combines, or "optimises" doses.
- Food-Grown® nutrients are taken with or after food unless the label states otherwise.
- Protocols should normally contain 1–4 products; fewer, well-rationalised products
  are preferred over long lists.
- Suggested review point for any protocol: 8–12 weeks, or sooner where symptoms change.
- Where two products contain overlapping nutrients (e.g. a multi plus a single mineral),
  the overlap must be pointed out in the rationale.
